title: Rework
author: Jason Fried, David Heinemeier Hansson
thesisParagraph: A durable small company can beat conventional business ritual by doing less, charging customers, shipping useful work, and protecting clarity. Growth, planning, fundraising, meetings, credentials, and corporate polish are treated as optional tools rather than default virtues.

signatureMoves: uses tiny chapters, short declarative rules, and anti-corporate reversals
treats planning, meetings, growth, and funding as suspect defaults
prefers useful product behavior over management theater
sounds like a founder deleting half the memo
uses short declarative chapter titles that sound like operating rules
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not make Rework sound like MBA process advice.
Do not romanticize venture capital, hypergrowth, or heroic overwork.
does not build academic literature reviews or long theoretical taxonomies

teachingArc: First and Takedowns clear away inherited assumptions about business scale, planning, failure, growth, and work. Go, Progress, Productivity, Competitors, and Evolution turn that skepticism into operating rules for starting, shipping, focusing attention, differentiating, and saying no. Promotion, Hiring, Damage Control, Culture, and Conclusion show how the same plainspoken discipline governs public attention, team design, customer trust, workplace norms, and immediate action.
forbiddenMoves: Do not defend business ritual unless the customer benefits.
Do not pad a Rework idea past its useful length.
